newsitem.title: USA: US foreign crudes seen languid except for Cusiana.
newsitem.headline: US foreign crudes seen languid except for Cusiana.

text.p: A Cusiana deal shook up an otherwise languid foreign crude market on the U.S. Gulf Coast on Tuesday as refiners worked to wrap up their September requirements, traders said.

Late on Monday, an equity producer placed a Cusiana cargo with a U.S. privately held company at 90 cents a barrel under November West Texas Intermediate/Cushing for September 24-25 loading, traders said.
The cargo was originally scheduled to load on September 19-23, but was pushed back along with most of the other September cargoes as a result of operational hiccups on the ground.
The deal confirms the somewhat higher price range for the Colombian grade, which moved several times last week at $1.05 to $1.10 under October WTI.
Another equity holder had the remaining September cargo loading September 28-29. The shipment was originally slated to load on September 23-27.
Colombian state oil company Ecopetrol had another cargo earlier slated to load on September 25-29, but this cargo had apparently slipped into October and was not heard actively offered.
Elsewhere in Latin America, traders were anticipating weaker levels for Venezuelan Mesa/Furrial crude in the October program, reflecting competition from newly released Iraqi barrels.
"Everyone's saying it's going to be cheaper. The question is how much cheaper," a Gulf trader said.
Venezuela sold all of its September cargoes of the coveted grade at between $2.45 and $2.65 under WTI, traders said.
"If I had to put a value on September, I'd say $2.60," a Gulf buyer said.

Meanwhile, traders were keeping an eye on yet another closure of Venezuela's key export route through prolific Lake Maracaibo. The route reopened to tanker traffic at 1500 local time/1900 GMT after a 17-hour closure due to a grounded dredger.
One U.S. buyer said his company was now lifting crude out of Bonaire and Puerto La Cruz to avoid the accident-prone lake route.
Elsewhere, Nigerian Forcados and Qua Iboe were heard offered at Dated Brent plus $1.90 and $1.80 a barrel, respectively, for early October delivery into the Gulf.
Finally, North Sea pickings remained scarce, with Brent notionally pegged at October WTI minus 25 cents a barrel.
Traders said the slim Brent/WTI spread and steep trans-Atlantic freight rates have kept North Sea crudes out of the Gulf.
